title: Quantile Lighthouse: p95/p99 telemetry per route, model, and region
creator: Sofia Ramos
description: Background: Teams have asked for high-fidelity quantile visibility split by HTTP route, model variant, and region to triage regressions quickly and correlate with traffic/throughput anomalies. Current rollups obscure hot-path regressions because they aggregate across models and regions. Goal: ship a compact, queryable p95/p99 telemetry grid ("Lighthouse") that supports fast explorer queries, actionable alerts, and pre-baked dashboards for SRE/Platform/Customer Success.
acceptance_criteria: Instrument p95 and p99 emitters at request ingress with labels: route, model_version, region, tenant_id (when available)
Store quantile rollups in the quantile-timeseries store with 1m granularity and 7d retention; support regrouping to 5m/1h in the query layer
Expose a Lighthouse API endpoint that returns p50/p95/p99 and token/sec for a given time window and dimension filters within <200ms for recent 1h windows
Create three dashboard views: overview (top regressions), route detail (top models for route), and model heatmap (region x route slice), with interactive drilldowns
Add regression watcher that raises P1 alert when p95 increases >25% and p99 increases >40% vs baseline for a sustained 10m window on any route+model+region slice
Documentation and runbook with triage steps and example queries; at least two smoke tests that simulate an injected latency regression and verify watcher alerts
work_items: Design quantile label schema and cardinality guardrails
Add instrumentation to frontdoor and routing layer to emit percentile metrics
Implement ingestion pipeline transform to create per-slice quantile rollups
Add query API and caching layer for Lighthouse explorer
Build Grafana dashboards and embed starter views in Console
Implement regression watcher job using baseline windows and deploy alerting rules
Smoke tests + load harness integration (tokens/sec measurement)
decisions: Use t-digest based rollups at 1m resolution to keep storage and compute bounded
Limit primary cardinality to route+model_version+region; tenant-level breakdowns behind a flag to avoid cardinality explosion
Baseline computation will use rolling 24h median of p95/p99 with weighting for time-of-day
tradeoffs: Fidelity vs cost: 1m rollups chosen instead of per-request storage to keep SLO for query latency
Cardinality constraints reduce signal for multi-tenant customers; adding tenant_id as opt-in solves customer debugability at cost of storage
Using an approximate quantile algorithm trades exactness for performance; acceptable for regression detection but not for per-request SLA guarantees
